My name is Jaimy. This is my son Aaron. We are from Thalayolaparambu, Kottayam. I am a member of the Jacobite Church. Now I am going into my testimony.
This is my son Aaron. From around the age of two or three, he began to show mild hyperactivity issues.
He started to be noticed. Even if it was small, at that age none of us make such a big deal of it.
But when he started attending some activities and a few small training classes, big complaints began to come in.
Like any mother, I got a bit upset. Since I myself work somewhat on the medical side, I knew there is no permanent cure for this.
I knew that; accepting it was very difficult. I showed him at the medical college and asked many doctors for their opinions.
I also asked the doctors at my workplace, and after talking to many people and trying to sort things out, even when medically diagnosed,
they told me there is no permanent cure — we can only continue with medication.
Because of what we know about medicines, and also because mentally we were not inclined toward that,
I decided not to do anything special. At that time a sister I work with gave me a newsletter of Kreupasanam.
But she didn’t say anything to me; she just handed the newspaper into my hands and said, “Try to visit that place” and left. Perhaps because of that,
I simply kept it in my hand and didn’t pay much attention to it. I had a feeling that that mother was not a stranger to me.
I was a person with full of deep devotion and love towards Mother. Even though I am a member of the Jacobite Church, I had mostly studied in convent schools,
so I knew prayers and the rosary, but after school those practices gradually left my hands.
Nevertheless, because I had great fondness and love for that mother, I thought I might as well go and see her. So I came here in 30th December 2021.
I didn’t know I had to take a covenant or write anything down; I hadn’t come knowing that. I didn’t know about writing any intentions or such.
Then, we all have a viewpoint, right? Do we need to say all this out loud so God will understand?
There’s that idea: “I have a plan for you; it is not for your destruction but for your welfare.”
Even then I felt these weren’t things we needed to persistently demand from God; everything that happens
is happening for good. A person who follows that perspective doesn’t go around forcefully demanding things from God.
I felt that it wasn’t something I needed to demand. So when this situation came, I came here, took the covenant, and inquired about the matters of the covenant. In a way,
I understood the matters. One thing I noticed is that it’s not mainly about prayer; within this, there are things to do. We have read in the Bible
that we must do acts of mercy, help others, and give what we have to those who don’t have.
But we don’t really do any of that, and likewise I didn’t do anything. I would just read and leave it. In meditation with the father, in our church meditations,
and in prayer meetings, all this is said; we hear it, but beyond that, there was no action. So when this came,
it felt like a logical package to me. Right then, I felt I had to tell what I received from the altar.
When I felt that, I thought, “God, the doctors tell me these things… if this is such a powerful package, then please let me know what is going to be done for me from there.”
I prayed for that; it was just a prayer in my heart. The intentions in the covenant, at that time, passed through our lives.
I wrote down a few things, thinking that God already knows everything. In particular, I wrote about my son.
After that, I didn’t show him to any other doctors. I didn’t buy any medicines that doctors had previously prescribed. And then I
prayed steadfastly to the Mother: “Mother, there is nothing impossible for you. There, in God’s presence, you should intercede for my son. This child has to live in this world;
please prepare the proper circumstances for him.” I prayed only that much. I didn’t say, “Change this, or I cannot bear it” or anything like that.
I continued like that. I gave the covenant items to my son. Even when he went to class, during periods before breaks,
this child would run around the classroom, cause problems, and there were countless complaints. Yet, in prayer,
he was first contained; he was with me while I prayed.
Moreover, it was a kind of light I received from the Mother. Because what I prayed, that was what happened. Not in other activities,
not when going outside or in other difficulties, I saw that this child was with me while I prayed.
I would give him the covenant items like honey and holy salt. Before going to school, I didn’t complain to anyone.
I didn’t tell anyone about this problem. Gradually, after renewing the covenant repeatedly,
I began to notice a significant change in this child. Later, when I went to the doctors, they asked me
whether I was giving all the medicine correctly. I said, “Doctor, I haven’t given any medicine at all until now.”
Then they asked, “Such a big change happened, how did this happen?” I said, “I have been given a powerful person, a physician in Christ Jesus,
through whom I can intercede, and he has done this for me.” They laughed a little,
but then as I went on, this child became a testimony to everyone around me. Even when I gave the newsletters or during missionary work,
I took this child along, letting everyone see the testimony. I would tell them, “This is my testimony; nothing else needs to be said.” Afterwards,
gradually in studies, other subjects, extracurricular activities, and church activities, in all such matters, he began to participate and
work independently with enthusiasm. Later, at the Holy Altar (in Jacobite church) — in our church, we call it the Holy Altar —
bringing my child, who previously was a very restless and problematic kid, to the altar for the service seemed impossible.
But now, without any trouble, my son has become a Altar boy who does properly at the Holy Altar. For me, as a mother,
there are many others who face far greater difficulties than this. So I firmly believe that this grace received by me, and this grace received by my son,
must be properly testified before God. One more thing: after I began praying about this matter,
I had the opportunity to meet many parents of children with autism and other difficulties, especially children who are specially abled,
and I was able to witness their struggles. This happened as a result of the providence of the Mother. Before that, I had never
had an opportunity to meet such people. Because of missionary work, even when I took my son with the newsletters and spoke to many people,
I was able to see children suffering in pain, distress, and difficulties without any remedy, and I was able to read testimony among them and bring them to faith. This is my first testimony.
The second is about my intentions. For 10 years, a small piece of land which has been idle without re-survey or paying the taxes.
As I was not in my hometown, I had to face these obstacles directly. Whenever we approached the office, they would say, “Nothing can be done immediately; come back later.”
But I realized that this land, which had been lying without re-survey and idle for 10 years, would become a problem, and it was necessary to take action. I was in the covenant,
so I had no fear. I prayed, “Mother, if this is God's will, let it happen.” While sitting like that, one day when I was working —
that day I was working from home — suddenly my laptop turned off. Nothing was wrong; the charge wasn’t finished, nothing at all.
Something like this had never happened before. Suddenly it turned off, the screen went blank, and immediately I felt someone inside me say,
“Let’s go visit the Tahsildar's office, the village office, one by one; anyway, it may have turned off.” It was a strong feeling.
No matter how much I tried, the laptop monitor wouldn’t turn on. I thought, “Let it be; I’ll go.” So I went straight.
When I reached there, the village officer was busy doing something, talking on the phone. I told the people in the office,
“I have an application; could you check it?” They looked at it and said, “There has been applications pending for two or three years here. Many people’s
applications are like this. Where did this come from now? Nothing will happen immediately; come back later.” I didn’t say anything and slowly walked out.
By the time I left, the village officer was free from the phone call. I just went inside. Wherever I went, I had holy salt, honey,
and holy oil with me. So I slowly took them from my bag and spoke to him. He gestured with his hand, telling me to sit.
I sat down, thinking in my heart, “Mother, let God's will be done here.” I put the
holy salt slowly under the table. Then suddenly he asked me, “What have you brought?” I said, “Sir, this is an application.”
He just read it and suddenly picked a pen from the ones on the table and began to write. When I looked, it
was a green pen with green ink. On the side of the application, he wrote something I didn’t understand, but he wrote it.
Immediately, he stood up. He is a person with a disability. He stood up for me and went to the
other officers. He gave the paper to the person who had earlier told me, “Come back later; nothing will happen now.”
After giving the paper, he didn’t say anything else. He just told me to leave the matter from here. I didn’t
say anything and left because the person had already told me in the first place, “Nothing will happen now; come back later.”
So I just stood near him, and immediately he said to me again, “Look, I have this…”
“Look at the file on the table where I’m sitting. These are all applications — pending for two or three years.”
Then he said, “I don’t think anything can be done if you just leave it there. Don’t have big expectations; go.” I replied, “Okay,” and said nothing.
I didn’t say anything and smiled. It was a Friday. The next day — Saturday/Sunday — on my way back from the church Mass,
I was coming through that area. I stopped the vehicle for a moment and thought in my heart, “Mother, if this is Your will and beneficial, and if it is done there for Your glory…”
“…I am ready to accept it.” That day my son was with me; I just…
…placed a little holy salt there. Before I reached home I received a call — it was the surveyor’s call. Who is a government official who calls on a Sunday?
Before I reached home after Sunday Mass, I got a call by the office who verified my name and address and said : "Tomorrow I’ll come to your place at 11:30. You must be present”
I was completely stunned. Who calls like that? And it was the surveyor himself calling my mobile. I had given no recommendation letter or anything to him.
All my blessings come from the Holy Mother — I accepted that. The next day he went, postponed his other surveys, and conducted the measurement at my place.
A week later I completed the other procedures, finalized everything, and it was registered — that was my second testimony.
I am not saying the Mother appeared visibly and did all this in front of me, but why did my monitor turn off while I was working?
Why did I go to that office at that time? Why was the village officer free then?
Why did another person say “this won’t happen,” and yet why did I feel inside a hope and assurance that it would happen — that the Mother would intervene?
All those things are signs of the Mother’s apparition.
Thirdly, I want to say: I work in a corporate field. There is a lot of stress and tension; not just an eight-hour job.
The stress and tension sometimes last until midnight. At that time, in my position, there were some difficulties.
I was not in a position to properly carry out missionary work and other acts of mercy. But I felt a duty to do them, and I prayed earnestly for that.
Then I received an insight.
The insight was that if I received a promotion or changed from this status, the situation would change and I would become somewhat free. I prayed for that.
Because even until then, my prayers were often interrupted. I must say, my prayers were often interrupted in the morning, at night, and in between.
But I really enjoyed carrying out the actions. I was investigating the ways I could properly complete the package of our covenant.
Later, as my father used to say, “Lower your status.” I thought, is this my status?
Is this job really my status? It has an income, so should I lower it? Should I let go of it completely to pursue holy work?
I was thinking like this because I had great confidence at that time. Based on the experiences I had received before, I considered this carefully.
I thought, what is needed, what is needed, what is needed. At that time, sitting there, this hard work — working 10 to 12 hours in front of the computer —
…if I said anything, I would have to explain the difficulties. If I needed to explain further, I would also have to mention my health problem. I have a condition called ocular myopathy.
It is a problem affecting the eye muscles. You can imagine, it is a situation where I cannot spend too much time in front of the computer or mobile.
It is not a vision problem, it is a muscle problem. It doesn’t go away. I had no complaints about it. Even now, it is not an impediment in my intentions.
It stays like that. It is not a problem. While working through it, that is when we gain strength, power, and a great testimony.
So, I started praying and dedicating for the promotion matter. There were some obstacles because I did not have enough time; it was not yet the time for the promotion.
But cutting through that time, the Holy Mother gave me a promotion. I did not submit any application anywhere, yet at the right time, She prepared it for me and freed me.
She made me free. Saturdays and Sundays were plenty enough. I work in Bangalore, which is a lot, but I could carry out the holy work.
That was how my third intention was accomplished.
For the fourth time, while considering that a change was needed in this work pattern, I received a notice through a friend: “Try this abroad if you can; it will work.”
Even then, we cannot grasp it fully. It is not about taking something from God forcibly. If it is harmful, it must move away from us.
So with that mindset, I dedicated it in the same mental state: “God, if this is good, let it happen. If not, remove it from me.”
I moved forward with this attitude. The first time, I ignored it because going abroad has many difficulties in various agencies.
So I let it go. But even then, it came again to me.
I slowly continued processing it. It is not yet completed. But before that, I had an exam called PT to write.
With such a tight schedule and work, I could not specially find time to study for it. I simply picked a date and prayed, taking that date.
After praying, a date came to my mind suddenly. But when I checked, it was a date two days past. I got it.
I got a schedule, but it was a date two days past. There was no time to study or prepare.
It didn’t matter. I trusted that the date was given by the Mother and accepted it as it was. Before entering the exam, before entering the exam,
I ate the holy honey properly. By “properly,” I mean I prayed and took a few drops. After that, while sitting there, it was a computer-based
exam. While sitting there, I kept praying. There is a speaking section, and what usually happens is,
while we speak, others sitting in nearby cubicles also speak. Their voices come over to us. What we say may not
be properly recorded, and sometimes we may get distracted by what they are saying. These are the challenges of such an exam.
That is exactly what happened. When I started speaking, a student in the neighboring cubicle started speaking loudly.
Accidentally, I also spoke at that moment, but I spoke in a good flow. What I realized that day was that
it was out of my hands. Yet, I didn’t feel tension. When we dedicate everything to God, why should we worry?
If it is meant for us, it will come to us. At that time, the candidate in the next cubicle said something, and I repeated it very clearly.
Among all the modules, the speaking section scored the highest marks: full marks, 90 out of 90. I only realized this
after returning home. Even then, I had confidence. If such a thing happens, there is a reason. I am not the one planning it.
I am the one executing the plan. What is meant to happen there is the Mother’s plan, arranged to glorify the Mother.
That exam happened in that way and succeeded. Then, many small and big daily needs and matters of our life
continued to pass by. We know and hear many things, but the disasters, difficulties, and crises that could knock us down in many ways
are moved away somehow. Knowing this happens not immediately, but eventually, is how many things in life work. There are many such matters.
Explaining everything would take too long. But that day, in 2021, I renewed the covenant properly. Whatever happened, even if I couldn’t
come here, I arranged for newsletters to be delivered through those who could come.
Since it was Bangalore, the newspaper wasn’t in Malayalam. I provided Kannada and Tamil editions. Regarding missionary work,
This is not an attitude we see here; for the people there, all of this is a great wonder — many of them have never even heard of these things.
Even though I don’t know Kannada very well, every newsletter I hand out contains these testimonies. I take the time to add updated testimonies each time I give a paper to a person.
I include the updated testimonies and spend that much time giving a newspaper to a person — handing it over, explaining it in a language they understand, be it English, Kannada, or Hindi.
I remember one Kannada-speaking family who said to me, “Is your life really this holy, living in Kerala?”
They asked whether even the minute things are observed in the way you pray.
At that time, covenant prayers in other languages had not been started here.
So I didn’t have the opportunity to tell them, “Listen to this.” But for those who needed English, I helped them via a YouTube channel so they could listen.
Their faith among us is greater — they have the disposition to sit quietly and listen patiently.
That became a great encouragement to me. When I went there I would take my son; whatever I said, I felt a desire to speak to them with evidence.
It wasn’t about saying something and just giving it; I wanted to answer their doubts precisely and clearly.
To do that I needed some knowledge and a divine discernment; without that, one could never speak in that way.
Because I had that eagerness, I carried out the missionary work with strength. Each time I spoke to someone, even though I did not know the language, somehow it was communicated.
When I saw their responses, I understood: not a single person refused to take the paper — everyone I spoke with and everyone I gave the paper to accepted it.
It wasn’t that I was distributing a huge number of papers; rather, the paper I gave was remarkably effective.
Whether Tamil or Kannada, later they began to ask me questions. Now, when I hand out the paper in that area, they respond loudly.
I speak before they take it.
In the beginning we were hesitant — we didn’t know what to say.
But once the paper is in our hands, we first read it. We read it, and inside it there is a concise form of what to say.
Most of the people who received the papers belong to other religions. I regularly distribute papers in that area, and there are even some who wait for me.
Then, when I was giving out papers in Kerala, I think it was a government officer who asked me, “God is Almighty, right? Then why didn’t He prevent the crucifixion and suffering?”
I asked him, “I haven’t prepared anything in advance, you know. I just came.”
Then, in my heart, I asked, “Mother, what should I say?”
And what I felt in my heart, that is what I said.
At first, he said to me, “Look, the tip box is full, and the newspaper of grace is there. I always keep it ready. So, what do you want to tell me?”
Seeing it as an opportunity, I said, “All advice isn’t from humans; it’s an example of what is needed.”
Often we don’t have what is needed. ‘Do this, do that, attain the kingdom of God,’ it says. But the covenant we can follow through action is the life I am leading.
When he asked what that action is, I said, “This is one of the actions. I am standing before you as a newsletter, participating in that action.”
He asked with more enthusiasm, “What does that mean?” I elaborated to him, explaining that the Holy Father could save His son there.
But how does the life cycle of an ordinary human go — through problems, difficulties, and joys?
The one who went through this era, who became flesh of the Word and incarnated on earth, born as a child from an ordinary mother, growing into a young man of 33 years —
Jesus Christ showed that life before us as evidence, speaking to us through the Bible.
Christ departed from us, and that is a model. I have not seen another such model. It is easy to advise or teach in a class,
but to show a life and teach how to face it — that is what He did, going to the cross and rising again.
In the name of Jesus Christ, this is what I give and speak to you. He remained silent for a while and
said to me, “It’s correct, even if you know something, even if I advise you now, you don’t have to follow it.”
“Okay, you are happy to talk this much; no one else spoke like this.”
It’s a small thing he said. That evening, when I walked back, I thought about what he said. I couldn’t remember everything.
Later, even if I tried to repeat it, I couldn’t. But at that time, I gave an answer to that question.
The missionary work continued very earnestly. Speaking of mercy work, when the covenant began,
after one renewal was done, the promotion came. Along with the promotion, the salary increment and some unexpected bonuses arrived.
I wasn’t aware of these things beforehand, but they came, and immediately I thought about what to do next.
I prayed to Mother, “Show me where and whom I should approach.” Then I got an opportunity to meet a sister working in a government hospital at the CHS.
She is a sister who goes into palliative care and visits homes.
Unexpectedly, he called me and said, “Didn’t you tell me earlier? There is a boy at a place — can you do something for him?”
So, to help, I went to see the boy. He and his mother had lost a child in
their early years. The boy is a Hindu, and he was lying down below a tree, weak and frail.
Then I asked, “Why have I come for this? What do you need?”
The boy told me, “I have been praying for a week, crying as I prayed. I need a customized wheelchair.”
I asked him if he knew about Mother. He said he had heard about Her but didn’t have much faith.
he asked how she would bless me in this condition. I said, “Haven’t you been praying for a week? Isn’t this a solution?”
The customized wheelchair was purchased — I didn’t buy it myself, but provided the funds. The boy came here one day in the wheelchair with his friends.
Due to the limitations of the covenant, his closest friend received the covenant on his behalf and carried out the mercy work for him.
Mercy activities continued in Bangalore. Some families with children were helped by providing household items, food, and other support.
Moreover, the work also included distributing Bibles and visiting nearby communities in a close and personal way.
Even though this was a simple approach, the significance of the Eucharist — the Mass — was something I deeply understood through
the covenant. During Mass, no matter the circumstances, distractions, or wandering thoughts, our attention is undisciplined.
Even if our church conducts excellent meditations, Bible teachings, or other group activities, the depth of the Mass is truly taught in the covenant life.
During Mass, not a single moment of attention should be lost. Every line spoken by the priest resonates within me.
I do not sit a Mass without consciously following it line by line. For the past year and a half, this has been my practice.
